Subject: Acme Health — POC trial planning recap & workload intake

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before the technical kickoff: 

What we discussed / requested items:
- Success criteria: define 2–3 measurable goals for the trial (latency targets, quality metrics on your evaluation set, and throughput). We'll capture these in the mutual action plan.
- Evaluation plan & ownership: you (Alex/Priya) will own the business evaluation; Redwood (David) will own infra/perf validation and instrumentation. Marissa will coordinate contracting/PO.
- Timeline: target 4-week internal POC after kick-off (kickoff proposed next Wed 11/17).
- Workload intake (please confirm numbers below):
  - Baseline steady-state RPS: 5 requests/sec
  - Expected average token length per request: ~120 tokens (typical chart-gen)
  - 95th token length: ~450 tokens (long reports)
  - Concurrency: 6–8 concurrent users hitting the service
  - Burst behavior: occasional spikes to ~50 RPS for ~30–60s (end of day batch preview)
  - SLA/latency expectations: desire p95 < 500ms, p99 ideally < 1s for interactive flows

Attachments I’m sending: workload intake template (acmehealth_workload_profile.xlsx) and initial success criteria doc for you to review.

Next steps:
1) Alex/Priya — confirm/adjust the workload numbers above and attach a small sample of typical requests (anonymized).
2) David — will propose recommended infra footprint and test plan once we get the sample.
3) Marissa — will prepare an MPA + draft PO language.

If anything above is off, flag it here and I’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

— Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the workload numbers below and adding a couple clarifications:

- Baseline steady-state RPS: 5 req/s (this is our current preview endpoint, roughly constant during the day)
- Average token length: 110–130 tokens (we measured 120 median)
- 95th token length: 420–500 tokens (occasional long reports)
- Concurrency: 6 active sessions typically; peak concurrency around 12 for internal load tests
- Burst patterns: yes — spikes to ~50 RPS for up to 45s happen when clinicians bulk-request summaries at shift changes; we sometimes see a few sustained bursts (20–30s) back to back during handoffs
- Data residency: all request/response payloads must remain in the US region (we're not sending PHI in the POC but prefer US-only processing)
- Model preference: we'd like to test an open Llama-based model you recommended plus a quantized variant if available

We will attach a 200-row sample of anonymized requests + expected outputs (Priya will drop in the Drive link) by EOD tomorrow. For success criteria, our business team will prioritize: 1) accuracy of summaries vs. human baseline (we'll provide evaluation rubric), 2) responsiveness (interactive feel), 3) stability under bursts.

Happy to join the kickoff on 11/17 — Alex

Thanks Alex — those numbers are helpful. A few notes from the infra/SE side and a proposed test plan: 

Quick infra recommendations (initial):
- Start with a small dedicated pool: 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs (or our hosted equivalent) to handle baseline + steady bursts; autoscale policy to add 1–2 nodes if queue latency exceeds threshold.
- Quantized model variant: we can test int8 quantized Llama variant; expect ~2–2.5x token/sec improvement, which helps with cost during bursts.
- Region enforcement: we'll pin the POC to our us-west region and disable cross-region fallbacks.

Proposed perf test plan (what we'll run after sample dataset is uploaded):
1) Baseline stability run — 30min at 5 RPS, measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
2) Burst replay — replay representative burst sequences (50 RPS for 45s, repeated 3x with 60s cool-down) to simulate clinician handoffs.
3) Concurrency stress — ramp to 12 concurrent sessions with random token length distribution drawn from your sample.
4) End-to-end quality check — run your evaluation rubric against 200-sample set, compute precision/recall/ROUGE (as applicable) and a human review pass for a 20-sample subset.

Initial success criteria suggestions (we can refine with your business team):
- Performance: p95 latency < 500ms, p99 < 1.2s during baseline; under burst we accept p95 up to 1s if throughput remains steady
- Stability: no request failure rate > 0.5% across tests
- Quality: automated eval metrics meet your rubric threshold (we suggest > 90% on extracted-key metric) and no major regression vs. baseline human score on the 20-sample review

Data collection & telemetry: we'll enable token-level traces, request/response sizes, and per-route cost telemetry. Please confirm any additional logs you need (we can redact payloads for privacy).

Questions for the Acme team:
- Do you have a preferred max memory per request (some long documents can exceed prompt windows)?
- For the quantized run — are you open to slightly different quality trade-offs if it reduces latency/cost materially?

Once Alex/Priya share the sample, I'll schedule the baseline run and share a runbook + Jenkins job we’ll use for the replay.

— David
David Kim
